headings.title: Request validation and transient API state

html:
Request validation and transient API state

The API models define input and response shapes and two small process-local stores. Payload validation checks what a caller supplied. Route admission captures accepted intent and resolves its owners; native execution decides whether work can proceed. Temporary UI records help present interactions and reuse observed terminal directories, but do not replace durable task, trace, permission or execution state.

See request lifecycle, prepared requests and durable task dispatch for the subsequent operations.

Public intent becomes validated input

flowchart TD Client[Public request body] --> Guards[Inherited public-input guards:<br/>routing overrides and root behavior internals] Guards --> Shape[Validate fields, bounds<br/>and behavior-effort choice] Shape --> Target[For Gateway request families,<br/>reconcile IDs, selection and scheduling intent] Target --> Consistent{Shape and intent consistent?} Consistent -->|No| Error[Return validation error before route work] Consistent -->|Yes| Route[Owning route accepts intent] Controls[Current server settings and authority] --> Route Route --> Accepted[Accepted request or durable task<br/>with context and identities] Accepted --> Native[Native admission and execution owners] Native --> Projection[Trace, task and response projections]

This is the ordinary public request/task path. Different payload families inherit different validators; the diagram is not a claim that every API body goes through every branch. Trusted internal callers can construct an already accepted payload without running public Pydantic validation. Their ordinary admission path still owns execution authority.

Contract What it establishes and what its owner still checks
QueueSubmission A bounded q_ identity, required nullable predecessor and optional digest. It forbids extra keys; it does not reserve a task or authorize dispatch.
BehaviorInput Public behavior effort. Its routing validator rejects reserved fields at the root and immediate context map; it is not a recursive scan of arbitrary data. Expanded behavior policies are rejected at the root. Retired top-level summarize_result is discarded for compatibility.
GatewayRequestInput Consistency between explicit Gateway ID/selection and context intent, plus validated scheduling preference. It copies context, normalizes selection and records its primary ID; registry resolution and target availability come later.
Direct request and preparation payloads Prompt, context, optional conversation/queue identity and policy choices. Their default mode is conversation. Preparation establishes timing/identity through its route rather than dispatching from the schema.
Durable task and monitor payloads Bounded saved intent. Their default mode is agent and start_now is true; acceptance, dependencies, availability and scheduling can still prevent immediate execution.
Confirmation and clarification payloads Explicit actions/answers and optional authority, operation, resource or choice identities. A supplied confirmation grant must agree with approve/deny. Native interaction owners still reject stale or mismatched replies.
Runtime-control payload A partial update whose unknown fields are forbidden. Shared validators check Memory mode, compact guidance, exact log capacity and provider overrides; parsing does not publish settings.
Availability and integration envelopes Typed observations and result projections. Constructing one does not test a target or complete execution; the producer owns those facts.
Gateway registration/update payloads Endpoint, label, optional node/default directory and enabled intent. Registry and transport owners perform registration, reachability and execution-scope work.

Omission and explicit null differ where a field validator demands a concrete value. For example, an omitted execution-log limit leaves the partial update unspecified, while a supplied null, boolean, fraction or zero is rejected. The shared capacity validator uses positive decimal strings so very large byte counts are not rounded by JSON/JavaScript numeric precision. It allocates no log storage.

The model-routing owner protects its reserved connection/configuration inputs. Provider override validation belongs to model configuration, which returns a detached validated map without filling omitted provider defaults. Settings persistence explains publication and checkpoint acknowledgement after validation. Interface appearance preferences have their existing schema and are outside this flow review.

Code request context snapshots

The server resolves a conversation's coding-thread binding before selecting the Code context policy. Public context cannot supply that binding, policy or rule-read coverage. Queue admission, direct requests and preparation capture the selected policy version; version 1 also captures the saved workspace-root AGENTS.md revision and complete content. Read errors prevent acceptance. A missing file is an explicit empty snapshot.

Accepted retries reuse that snapshot, including after rollout or rollback. Continuation and recovery retain it with the current task's instructions, operation receipts and rule-page coverage. New requests alone receive newly saved rules and the currently selected policy. SRE does not enter this path. The workspace manual describes the opt-in rollout, bounded recent history and thread-scoped retrieval interface.

Temporary request projections

flowchart TD Route[Accepted request route] --> Create[Create local request projection] Create --> Fence{Request fenced, or deleted chat<br/>without independent task exception?} Fence -->|Yes| Ignore[Keep projection absent] Fence -->|No| Map[Locked access-ordered request map] Map --> Limit[Evict least-recently-used entries<br/>above configured bound] Native[Native result and wait presentation] --> Finish[Update existing interaction fields<br/>when not a suspended result] Finish --> Map Map --> Read[Return shallow detached projection<br/>and refresh recency] Read --> Caller[UI/lineage caller] Caller --> Authority[Revalidate through durable<br/>native/trace owners when required] Handled[Handled flag or child-link update] --> Map Delete[Conversation cleanup] --> Tombstones[Retain request/conversation fences] Delete --> Remove[Remove supplied request identities] Remove --> Map Tombstones --> Fence

AgentUiRequestStateStore defaults to 100 recent entries and clamps a configured limit to at least one. It uses an RLock and access-ordered OrderedDict. Creation copies the outer context, replaces any existing projection for that request and evicts the least recently used entries. Eviction does not cancel work or delete native history. The separate deletion-fence sets are process-local and are not bounded by the recent-entry limit.

discard_conversation records the conversation and supplied request IDs as deleted, then removes those request projections. A fenced request ID cannot be recreated. A fenced conversation can still have a new independent task_sheet or scheduled_event projection; ordinary chat request recreation remains blocked. These checks are specific to this local store. The durable deletion/continuation owners enforce their own fences.

get returns a new dataclass with one-level copies of context, action dictionaries and the clarification dictionary. Nested values are not recursively detached. finish updates native-run and interaction presentation only when the entry still exists. It preserves existing handled flags and lineage. Marking an interaction handled is local bookkeeping; it neither approves a command nor applies an answer.

Continuation lookup searches from most recently accessed matching child state, which is not necessarily chronological creation order. The request lifecycle's lineage helper falls back to retained trace relationships when local state has no child or parent. That fallback belongs to the caller, not to the local store.

The native response adapter updates interaction presentation for non-suspended results. Paused/resource/job/event waits can retain native state without calling this local finish path. Missing UI state therefore cannot establish that execution or a pending interaction disappeared.

Terminal working-directory observations

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Request context owner participant Store as Terminal session store participant Paths as Controller path resolver Caller->>Store: Compare session ID, directory and optional target IDs alt Blank input, missing session or conflicting supplied target Store-->>Caller: No trusted directory else Session carries Gateway identity Store->>Store: Compare exact target-native directory text Store-->>Caller: Matching stored directory or no match else Session has no Gateway identity Store->>Paths: Expand home and resolve both paths without requiring existence Paths-->>Store: Resolved paths or resolution error Store-->>Caller: Equal resolved directory or no match end alt Trusted directory returned Caller->>Caller: Retain terminal identity, directory and execution intent else No match Caller->>Caller: Remove terminal session, directory and execution intent end Note over Caller,Paths: Comparison opens no terminal and proves no remote path exists

AgentTerminalSessionStore also defaults to 100 access-ordered observations. create generates an identity and UTC timestamps from the supplied directory and target; it returns the same mutable record held in the store. update_cwd ignores blank or missing identities, updates an existing observation and returns a detached dataclass copy. Callers must establish the authority of the reported directory. Neither method contacts the Gateway.

trusted_cwd rejects a Gateway ID/node mismatch when both supplied and stored values are nonempty. Omitted target fields do not independently reject the request. If the session contains either target identity, its directory comparison is exact; a Windows Gateway path is not resolved as a Controller-local path. For an unbound session, both paths use local expanduser().resolve(strict=False) and must match. Resolution errors return no match. A match updates recency; eviction only removes the observation and does not close the real terminal.

_apply_trusted_terminal_context keeps terminal context only after this comparison. On failure it removes terminal_session_id, terminal_cwd and execute_in_terminal. Later admission still resolves target authority and validates execution; this local comparison is not a general filesystem-access grant.

Verification

Selected isolated tests cover exact log capacities, recovery deadline boundaries, target-native terminal paths, deleted request fencing and public model-routing overrides. All 26 selected cases pass with temporary stores and fixture authorities. They do not exercise live model inference or production Gateway operations. Full Python AST comparison preserves all model fields, validators, literals and runtime docstrings during this documentation change; the checks do not certify every possible payload or continuation race.
